svg.text: A deliberate detent acts before the cap can release
Actual XZ section through the rear spring / fixed pins. Green rotor · blue fixed pins. Red = blocked rigid overlap.
LOCK · spring rests in its pocket
The curved spring is part of the flat-printed wheel. Its outer relief frees radial movement.
Nominal radial movement: 0.35 mm. Resting pockets unload the spring at LOCK and OPEN.
The small inner peg/track sets travel limits; the larger outer pin provides the detent.
At 5°, 10° and 15° the detent is engaged while the cap is still captured by the nose.
The shoulder axle can be seated firmly without squeezing the wheel to create friction.
The red region must be accommodated by spring bending in a print. It is not permitted rigid interpenetration.
This establishes a designed release barrier, not a measured torque or a bag-shake rating.
If the real wheel turns freely, does not return or cracks, revise the spring; do not compensate by clamping the axle.
A matching 70 mm closed-ended sample preserves this mechanism and both production print orientations.
Use PLA for the trial and the stock M6 nut. Printed M6 thread fit must be tried gently before assembly.
